sanskrit: sa hatāśvād avaplutya rathād vai rathināṃ varaḥ khaḍgam ādāya niśitaṃ vimalaṃ ca śarāvaram śyenavad vyacarat kruddhaḥ śikhaṇḍī śatrutāpanaḥ
english: Leaping down from his car whose horses were slain, that foremost of chariot-warriors, Śikhaṇḍī, tormentor of foes, took up a keen-edged sword and a bright shield, and in his wrath ranged over the field like a hawk.

sanskrit: sakhaḍgasya mahārāja caratas tasya saṃyuge nāntaraṃ dadṛśe drauṇis tad adbhutam ivābhavat
english: As he moved through the battle, sword in hand, O great king, the son of Droṇa could descry no opening in him; and that seemed a marvel indeed.

sanskrit: tataḥ śarasahasrāṇi bahūni bharatarṣabha preṣayām āsa samare drauṇiḥ paramakopanaḥ
english: Then, O bull of the Bhāratas, the son of Droṇa, kindled to utmost fury, loosed many thousands of arrows in that fray.

sanskrit: tām āpatantīṃ samare śaravṛṣṭiṃ sudāruṇām asinā tīkṣṇadhāreṇa ciccheda balināṃ varaḥ
english: But that most terrible shower of arrows, descending upon him in battle, the foremost of the mighty cut apart with his sharp-edged sword.

sanskrit: tato 'sya vimalaṃ drauṇiḥ śatacandraṃ manoramam carmācchinad asiṃ cāsya khaṇḍayām āsa saṃyuge śitaiḥ subahuśo rājaṃs taṃ ca vivyādha patribhiḥ
english: Then the son of Droṇa shattered his bright and lovely shield, blazoned with a hundred moons, and broke his sword in the encounter; and with his keen shafts, O king, he pierced him again and again.

sanskrit: śikhaṇḍī tu tataḥ khaḍgaṃ khaṇḍitaṃ tena sāyakaiḥ āvidhya vyasṛjat tūrṇaṃ jvalantam iva pannagam
english: Thereupon Śikhaṇḍī, brandishing the sword that had been broken by those arrows, swiftly hurled it like a blazing serpent.

sanskrit: tam āpatantaṃ sahasā kālānalasamaprabham ciccheda samare drauṇir darśayan pāṇilāghavam śikhaṇḍinaṃ ca vivyādha śarair bahubhir āyasaiḥ
english: As it flew at him suddenly, bright as the fire of doom, the son of Droṇa cut it in the air, displaying his deftness of hand, and pierced Śikhaṇḍī with many shafts of iron.

sanskrit: śikhaṇḍī tu bhṛśaṃ rājaṃs tāḍyamānaḥ śitaiḥ śaraiḥ āruroha rathaṃ tūrṇaṃ mādhavasya mahātmanaḥ
english: Then Śikhaṇḍī, O king, sorely smitten by those keen shafts, swiftly mounted the chariot of the high-souled Mādhava.

sanskrit: sātyakis tu tataḥ kruddho rākṣasaṃ krūram āhave alambusaṃ śarair ghorair vivyādha balinaṃ balī
english: Then Sātyaki, in wrath, that mighty one, pierced with dreadful arrows in the fray the cruel and powerful Rākṣasa Alambusa.

sanskrit: rākṣasendras tatas tasya dhanuś ciccheda bhārata ardhacandreṇa samare taṃ ca vivyādha sāyakaiḥ māyāṃ ca rākṣasīṃ kṛtvā śaravarṣair avākirat
english: Then that lord of the Rākṣasas, O Bhārata, severed his bow with a crescent-headed shaft, pierced him with arrows in the battle, and, weaving a Rākṣasa illusion, overwhelmed him with showers of darts.

sanskrit: tatrādbhutam apaśyāma śaineyasya parākramam nāsaṃbhramad yat samare vadhyamānaḥ śitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Therein we beheld a marvel of valor in the grandson of Śini: even while struck down by keen shafts in the battle, he was not dismayed.

sanskrit: aindram astraṃ ca vārṣṇeyo yojayām āsa bhārata vijayād yad anuprāptaṃ mādhavena yaśasvinā
english: Then the scion of the Vṛṣṇis fitted to his bow the weapon of Indra, O Bhārata, which the illustrious Mādhava had obtained from Vijaya.

sanskrit: tad astraṃ bhasmasāt kṛtvā māyāṃ tāṃ rākṣasīṃ tadā alambusaṃ śarair ghorair abhyākirata sarvaśaḥ parvataṃ vāridhārābhiḥ prāvṛṣīva balāhakaḥ
english: That weapon reduced the Rākṣasa illusion to ashes; and then he covered Alambusa on every side with dreadful shafts, as a rain-cloud in the wet season drenches a mountain with its streams of water.

sanskrit: tat tathā pīḍitaṃ tena mādhavena mahātmanā pradudrāva bhayād rakṣo hitvā sātyakim āhave
english: Thus afflicted by the high-souled Mādhava, the demon fled in terror, abandoning Sātyaki in the fight.

sanskrit: tam ajeyaṃ rākṣasendraṃ saṃkhye maghavatā api śaineyaḥ prāṇadaj jitvā yodhānāṃ tava paśyatām
english: Having vanquished that lord of the Rākṣasas, whom even Maghavat could not conquer in battle, the grandson of Śini roared aloud, while your warriors looked on.

sanskrit: nyahanat tāvakāṃś cāpi sātyakiḥ satyavikramaḥ niśitair bahubhir bāṇais te 'dravanta bhayārditāḥ
english: And Sātyaki, of true prowess, slew your men with many keen arrows; afflicted with terror, they fled.

sanskrit: etasminn eva kāle tu drupadasyātmajo balī dhṛṣṭadyumno mahārāja tava putraṃ janeśvaram chādayām āsa samare śaraiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ
english: At that very moment, O great king, the mighty son of Drupada, Dhṛṣṭadyumna, covered your son, that lord of men, with straight-jointed arrows in the battle.

sanskrit: saṃchādyamāno viśikhair dhṛṣṭadyumnena bhārata vivyathe na ca rājendra tava putro janeśvaraḥ
english: Though shrouded by the shafts of Dhṛṣṭadyumna, O Bhārata, your son, that lord of men, O king of kings, was not shaken.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnaṃ ca samare tūrṇaṃ vivyādha sāyakaiḥ ṣaṣṭyā ca triṃśatā caiva tad adbhutam ivābhavat
english: Swiftly he pierced Dhṛṣṭadyumna in battle with sixty and then with thirty arrows; and that seemed a marvel.

sanskrit: tasya senāpatiḥ kruddho dhanuś ciccheda māriṣa hayāṃś ca caturaḥ śīghraṃ nijaghāna mahārathaḥ śaraiś cainaṃ suniśitaiḥ kṣipraṃ vivyādha saptabhiḥ
english: Then his commander, that mighty car-warrior, in wrath severed his bow, O sire, and swiftly slew his four horses, and quickly pierced him with seven keen-edged shafts.

sanskrit: sa hatāśvān mahābāhur avaplutya rathād balī padātir asim udyamya prādravat pārṣataṃ prati
english: The mighty-armed one, his horses slain, leapt down from his chariot, and on foot, raising his sword, rushed at the son of Pṛṣata.

sanskrit: śakunis taṃ samabhyetya rājagṛddhī mahābalaḥ rājānaṃ sarvalokasya ratham āropayat svakam
english: Then Śakuni, of great might, eager for the king's safety, came up and lifted that lord of all the world onto his own car.

sanskrit: tato nṛpaṃ parājitya pārṣataḥ paravīrahā nyahanat tāvakaṃ sainyaṃ vajrapāṇir ivāsuram
english: Then the son of Pṛṣata, slayer of hostile heroes, having defeated the king, fell upon your host as the wielder of the thunderbolt fell upon the Asuras.

sanskrit: kṛtavarmā raṇe bhīmaṃ śarair ārchan mahāratham pracchādayām āsa ca taṃ mahāmegho raviṃ yathā
english: In the battle Kṛtavarman assailed the great car-warrior Bhīma with arrows, and shrouded him as a vast cloud shrouds the sun.

sanskrit: tataḥ prahasya samare bhīmasenaḥ paraṃtapaḥ preṣayām āsa saṃkruddhaḥ sāyakān kṛtavarmaṇe
english: Then, smiling in the fray, Bhīmasena, scorcher of foes, in great wrath loosed his arrows at Kṛtavarman.

sanskrit: tair ardyamāno 'tirathaḥ sātvataḥ śastrakovidaḥ nākampata mahārāja bhīmaṃ cārchac chitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Though tormented by them, that surpassing car-warrior of the Sātvatas, skilled in arms, did not falter, O great king, but struck Bhīma in turn with keen shafts.

sanskrit: tasyāśvāṃś caturo hatvā bhīmaseno mahābalaḥ sārathiṃ pātayām āsa dhvajaṃ ca supariṣkṛtam
english: Then Bhīmasena of great might slew his four horses, brought down his charioteer, and felled his richly adorned banner.

sanskrit: śarair bahuvidhaiś cainam ācinot paravīrahā śakalīkṛtasarvāṅgaḥ śvāvidvat samadṛśyata
english: And that slayer of hostile heroes covered him with arrows of many kinds, so that, his whole body bristling, he looked like a porcupine.

sanskrit: hatāśvāt tu rathāt tūrṇaṃ vṛṣakasya rathaṃ yayau syālasya te mahārāja tava putrasya paśyataḥ
english: Then, leaving his car whose steeds were slain, he swiftly went over to the chariot of Vṛṣaka, your brother-in-law, O great king, while your son looked on.

sanskrit: bhīmaseno 'pi saṃkruddhas tava sainyam upādravat nijaghāna ca saṃkruddho daṇḍapāṇir ivāntakaḥ
english: And Bhīmasena too, exceedingly wrathful, charged upon your host, and in his fury smote it down like Death himself, staff in hand.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca bahūnīha vicitrāṇi dvairathāni sma saṃjaya pāṇḍūnāṃ māmakaiḥ sārdham aśrauṣaṃ tava jalpataḥ
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: Many and various single combats between the Pāṇḍavas and my own men have I heard of from you, Saṃjaya, as you tell your tale.

sanskrit: na caiva māmakaṃ kaṃ cid dhṛṣṭaṃ śaṃsasi saṃjaya nityaṃ pāṇḍusutān hṛṣṭān abhagnāṃś caiva śaṃsasi
english: Yet you tell me of not one of my own as elated, O Saṃjaya; ever you describe the sons of Pāṇḍu as joyous and unbroken.

sanskrit: jīyamānān vimanaso māmakān vigataujasaḥ vadase saṃyuge sūta diṣṭam etad asaṃśayam
english: My own you describe as worsted, dispirited, and bereft of vigor in the battle, O sūta; this is surely the work of fate, beyond doubt.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca yathāśakti yathotsāhaṃ yuddhe ceṣṭanti tāvakāḥ darśayānāḥ paraṃ śaktyā pauruṣaṃ puruṣarṣabha
english: Saṃjaya said: According to their strength and according to their zeal your men strive in the fight, showing their manhood to the utmost of their power, O bull among men.

sanskrit: gaṅgāyāḥ suranadyā vai svādubhūtaṃ yathodakam mahodadhiguṇābhyāsāl lavaṇatvaṃ nigacchati
english: As the sweet water of Gaṅgā, the river of the gods, by long contact with the nature of the great ocean comes to take on saltiness,

sanskrit: tathā tat pauruṣaṃ rājaṃs tāvakānāṃ mahātmanām prāpya pāṇḍusutān vīrān vyarthaṃ bhavati saṃyuge
english: even so, O king, does the prowess of your high-souled warriors, on meeting the heroic sons of Pāṇḍu, come to nothing in the battle.

sanskrit: ghaṭamānān yathāśakti kurvāṇān karma duṣkaram na doṣeṇa kuruśreṣṭha kauravān gantum arhasi
english: They labor to the limit of their power and perform deeds hard to achieve; you should not, O best of the Kurus, lay blame upon the Kauravas.

sanskrit: tavāparādhāt sumahān saputrasya viśāṃ pate pṛthivyāḥ prakṣayo ghoro yamarāṣṭravivardhanaḥ
english: It is through your fault, and your son's, O lord of peoples, that this dread and mighty destruction of the earth, that swells the realm of Yama, has come to pass.

sanskrit: ātmadoṣāt samutpannaṃ śocituṃ nārhase nṛpa na hi rakṣanti rājānaḥ sarvārthān nāpi jīvitam
english: It has sprung from your own fault, and you ought not to grieve, O king; for kings can guard neither all their interests nor even their lives.

sanskrit: yuddhe sukṛtināṃ lokān icchanto vasudhādhipāḥ camūṃ vigāhya yudhyante nityaṃ svargaparāyaṇāḥ
english: Desiring the worlds reserved for the doers of good deeds, the lords of earth plunge into the host and fight, ever intent upon heaven.

sanskrit: pūrvāhṇe tu mahārāja prāvartata janakṣayaḥ tan mamaikamanā bhūtvā śṛṇu devāsuropamam
english: In the forenoon, O great king, the slaughter of men began; with single mind hear of it from me, for it was like the war of gods and demons.

sanskrit: āvantyau tu maheṣvāsau mahātmānau mahābalau irāvantam abhiprekṣya sameyātāṃ raṇotkaṭau teṣāṃ pravavṛte yuddhaṃ tumulaṃ lomaharṣaṇam
english: The two princes of Avanti, mighty bowmen, high-souled and of great strength, fierce in war, beholding Irāvat, advanced upon him; and there began among them a tumultuous battle that made the hair stand on end.

sanskrit: irāvāṃs tu susaṃkruddho bhrātarau devarūpiṇau vivyādha niśitais tūrṇaṃ śaraiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ tāv enaṃ pratyavidhyetāṃ samare citrayodhinau
english: Irāvat, sorely enraged, swiftly pierced the two godlike brothers with keen, straight-jointed shafts; and those two, fighters of varied skill, pierced him in turn in the fray.

sanskrit: yudhyatāṃ hi tathā rājan viśeṣo na vyadṛśyata yatatāṃ śatrunāśāya kṛtapratikṛtaiṣiṇām
english: As they fought thus, O king, no difference could be seen between them, as they strove for the destruction of the foe, each seeking to repay stroke for stroke.

sanskrit: irāvāṃs tu tato rājann anuvindasya sāyakaiḥ caturbhiś caturo vāhān anayad yamasādanam
english: Then Irāvat, O king, with four arrows sent the four steeds of Anuvinda to the abode of Yama.

sanskrit: bhallābhyāṃ ca sutīkṣṇābhyāṃ dhanuḥ ketuṃ ca māriṣa ciccheda samare rājaṃs tad adbhutam ivābhavat
english: And with two exceedingly sharp broad-headed shafts he severed his bow and his banner in the battle, O sire; and that, O king, seemed a marvel.

sanskrit: tyaktvānuvindo 'tha rathaṃ vindasya ratham āsthitaḥ dhanur gṛhītvā navamaṃ bhārasādhanam uttamam
english: Then Anuvinda, abandoning his own car, mounted the chariot of Vinda, and took up a new bow, excellent and able to bear a heavy strain.

sanskrit: tāv ekasthau raṇe vīrāv āvantyau rathināṃ varau śarān mumucatus tūrṇam irāvati mahātmani
english: Then the two heroes of Avanti, foremost of car-warriors, standing together upon one car, swiftly loosed their arrows at the high-souled Irāvat.

sanskrit: tābhyāṃ muktā mahāvegāḥ śarāḥ kāñcanabhūṣaṇāḥ divākarapathaṃ prāpya chādayām āsur ambaram
english: The arrows loosed by them, gold-adorned and of great speed, reaching the path of the sun, covered over the sky.

sanskrit: irāvāṃs tu tataḥ kruddho bhrātarau tau mahārathau vavarṣa śaravarṣeṇa sārathiṃ cāpy apātayat
english: Then Irāvat in wrath rained a shower of arrows upon those two great car-warriors, the brothers, and struck down their charioteer as well.

sanskrit: tasmin nipatite bhūmau gatasattve 'tha sārathau rathaḥ pradudrāva diśaḥ samudbhrāntahayas tataḥ
english: And when the charioteer had fallen lifeless to the ground, the chariot, its horses now maddened and bolting, rushed off in every direction.

sanskrit: tau sa jitvā mahārāja nāgarājasutāsutaḥ pauruṣaṃ khyāpayaṃs tūrṇaṃ vyadhamat tava vāhinīm
english: Having vanquished those two, O great king, the son of the daughter of the serpent-king, proclaiming his manhood, swiftly scattered your host.

sanskrit: sā vadhyamānā samare dhārtarāṣṭrī mahācamūḥ vegān bahuvidhāṃś cakre viṣaṃ pītveva mānavaḥ
english: That great host of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son, smitten in the battle, reeled in many ways, like a man who has drunk poison.

sanskrit: haiḍimbo rākṣasendras tu bhagadattaṃ samādravat rathenādityavarṇena sadhvajena mahābalaḥ
english: Then the Rākṣasa lord, son of Hiḍimbā, of great might, rushed upon Bhagadatta in his sun-colored car with its banner.

sanskrit: tataḥ prāgjyotiṣo rājā nāgarājaṃ samāsthitaḥ yathā vajradharaḥ pūrvaṃ saṃgrāme tārakāmaye
english: Then the king of Prāgjyotiṣa, mounted upon his lordly elephant, came on as did the wielder of the thunderbolt of old in the war over Tārakā.

sanskrit: tatra devāḥ sagandharvā ṛṣayaś ca samāgatāḥ viśeṣaṃ na sma vividur haiḍimbabhagadattayoḥ
english: There the gods with the Gandharvas and the seers, gathered together, could find no difference between the son of Hiḍimbā and Bhagadatta.

sanskrit: yathā surapatiḥ śakras trāsayām āsa dānavān tathaiva samare rājaṃs trāsayām āsa pāṇḍavān
english: As Śakra, lord of the gods, struck terror into the Dānavas, even so in the battle, O king, did he strike terror into the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: tena vidrāvyamāṇās te pāṇḍavāḥ sarvatodiśam trātāraṃ nābhyavindanta sveṣv anīkeṣu bhārata
english: Routed by him on every side, those Pāṇḍava warriors, O Bhārata, could find no protector among their own ranks.

sanskrit: bhaimaseniṃ rathasthaṃ tu tatrāpaśyāma bhārata śeṣā vimanaso bhūtvā prādravanta mahārathāḥ
english: There we saw only the son of Bhīmasena standing upon his car, O Bhārata; the rest of the great car-warriors, despairing, fled away.

sanskrit: nivṛtteṣu tu pāṇḍūnāṃ punaḥ sainyeṣu bhārata āsīn niṣṭānako ghoras tava sainyeṣu saṃyuge
english: But when the troops of the Pāṇḍavas had rallied once more, O Bhārata, a terrible din arose among your troops in the battle.

sanskrit: ghaṭotkacas tato rājan bhagadattaṃ mahāraṇe śaraiḥ pracchādayām āsa meruṃ girim ivāmbudaḥ
english: Then Ghaṭotkaca, O king, in that great fight covered Bhagadatta with arrows, as a rain-cloud covers Mount Meru.

sanskrit: nihatya tāñ śarān rājā rākṣasasya dhanuścyutān bhaimaseniṃ raṇe tūrṇaṃ sarvamarmasv atāḍayat
english: Striking down those shafts of the Rākṣasa loosed from the bow, the king swiftly smote the son of Bhīmasena in all his vital parts.

sanskrit: sa tāḍyamāno bahubhiḥ śaraiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ na vivyathe rākṣasendro bhidyamāna ivācalaḥ
english: Though smitten by many straight-jointed shafts, that lord of the Rākṣasas was not shaken, like a mountain being cleft.

sanskrit: tasya prāgjyotiṣaḥ kruddhas tomarān sa caturdaśa preṣayām āsa samare tāṃś ca ciccheda rākṣasaḥ
english: At him the king of Prāgjyotiṣa in wrath hurled fourteen lances in the battle; and the Rākṣasa cut them all asunder.

sanskrit: sa tāṃś chittvā mahābāhus tomarān niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ bhagadattaṃ ca vivyādha saptatyā kaṅkapatribhiḥ
english: Having cut down those lances with his keen shafts, the mighty-armed one pierced Bhagadatta with seventy heron-feathered arrows.

sanskrit: tataḥ prāgjyotiṣo rājan prahasann iva bhārata tasyāśvāṃś caturaḥ saṃkhye pātayām āsa sāyakaiḥ
english: Then the king of Prāgjyotiṣa, as if smiling, O Bhārata, struck down his four horses in the battle with his arrows.

sanskrit: sa hatāśve rathe tiṣṭhan rākṣasendraḥ pratāpavān śaktiṃ cikṣepa vegena prāgjyotiṣagajaṃ prati
english: Standing upon his car whose steeds were slain, that valiant lord of the Rākṣasas hurled a dart with force at the elephant of the Prāgjyotiṣa king.

sanskrit: tām āpatantīṃ sahasā hemadaṇḍāṃ suvegitām tridhā ciccheda nṛpatiḥ sā vyakīryata medinīm
english: As it flew suddenly at him, that gold-shafted dart of great speed, the king cut it in three, and it fell scattered upon the earth.

sanskrit: śaktiṃ vinihatāṃ dṛṣṭvā haiḍimbaḥ prādravad bhayāt yathendrasya raṇāt pūrvaṃ namucir daityasattamaḥ
english: Seeing his dart struck down, the son of Hiḍimbā fled in fear, as Namuci, best of the Daityas, fled of old from the battle with Indra.

sanskrit: taṃ vijitya raṇe śūraṃ vikrāntaṃ khyātapauruṣam ajeyaṃ samare rājan yamena varuṇena ca
english: Having vanquished in battle that hero, valiant and of famed manhood, unconquerable in war, O king, even by Yama and by Varuṇa,

sanskrit: pāṇḍavīṃ samare senāṃ saṃmamarda sakuñjaraḥ yathā vanagajo rājan mṛdnaṃś carati padminīm
english: with his elephant he trampled down the Pāṇḍava host in the battle, as a wild elephant, O king, ranges crushing a bed of lotuses.

sanskrit: madreśvaras tu samare yamābhyāṃ saha saṃgataḥ svasrīyau chādayāṃ cakre śaraughaiḥ pāṇḍunandanau
english: Then the lord of the Madras, joining battle with the twins, covered with floods of arrows those two sons of Pāṇḍu, his sister's sons.

sanskrit: sahadevas tu samare mātulaṃ vīkṣya saṃgatam avārayac charaugheṇa megho yadvad divākaram
english: But Sahadeva in the battle, beholding his maternal uncle come to grips with him, warded him off with a flood of arrows, as a cloud screens the sun.

sanskrit: chādyamānaḥ śaraugheṇa hṛṣṭarūpataro 'bhavat tayoś cāpy abhavat prītir atulā mātṛkāraṇāt
english: Covered by that flood of arrows, he grew all the more joyful in his bearing; and between those two there arose, for their mother's sake, a love beyond compare.

sanskrit: tataḥ prahasya samare nakulasya mahārathaḥ aśvān vai caturo rājaṃś caturbhiḥ sāyakottamaiḥ preṣayām āsa samare yamasya sadanaṃ prati
english: Then, smiling in the fray, that great car-warrior, O king, sent the four horses of Nakula with four excellent arrows to the abode of Yama.

sanskrit: hatāśvāt tu rathāt tūrṇam avaplutya mahārathaḥ āruroha tato yānaṃ bhrātur eva yaśasvinaḥ
english: Then that great car-warrior, swiftly leaping down from his car whose steeds were slain, mounted the vehicle of his own illustrious brother.

sanskrit: ekasthau tu raṇe śūrau dṛḍhe vikṣipya kārmuke madrarājarathaṃ kruddhau chādayām āsatuḥ kṣaṇāt
english: Then the two heroes, standing together upon one car, drawing their stout bows in wrath, in a moment covered over the chariot of the king of the Madras.

sanskrit: sa cchādyamāno bahubhiḥ śaraiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ svasrīyābhyāṃ naravyāghro nākampata yathācalaḥ prahasann iva tāṃ cāpi śaravṛṣṭiṃ jaghāna ha
english: Though covered by many straight-jointed shafts from his sister's sons, that tiger among men did not waver, like a mountain; and, as if smiling, he beat back that very shower of arrows.

sanskrit: sahadevas tataḥ kruddhaḥ śaram udyamya vīryavān madrarājam abhiprekṣya preṣayām āsa bhārata
english: Then Sahadeva, the valiant, in wrath, raising a shaft and fixing his gaze on the king of the Madras, sped it forth, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: sa śaraḥ preṣitas tena garutmān iva vegavān madrarājaṃ vinirbhidya nipapāta mahītale
english: That arrow, sped by him, swift as Garutmat, pierced through the king of the Madras and fell upon the surface of the earth.
